name: Dyula
notes: Standard Dyula (Jula) Latin orthography as used in Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso (Braconnier & Diané 1982; DNAFLA-derived Manding conventions shared with Bambara). Nasal vowels are written with a vowel followed by ⟨n⟩ (⟨an⟩, ⟨en⟩, ⟨in⟩, ⟨on⟩, ⟨ɔn⟩, ⟨ɛn⟩, ⟨un⟩): each spells one nasalized vowel nucleus, not vowel+consonant (AGENTS.md test 1 — the phonemic value is not the concatenation of the oral vowel and /n/). ⟨ny⟩, ⟨gb⟩ and ⟨kp⟩ are true digraphs for the single segments /ɲ/, /ɡb/, /kp/ (labial-velars and the palatal nasal are not sequences in Manding phonology). ⟨c⟩ and ⟨j⟩ represent the palatal affricates /t̠ʃ/ and /d̠ʒ/. Dyula is tonal (two-tone system, PHOIBLE 696); tone is not consistently marked in everyday orthography and is left unencoded here — a documented exemption distinct from lexical stress, which Manding varieties do not contrast phonemically.
